deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is not a Riemann manuscript. It is the last page of a private letter signed 'R. Dedekind', dated 'Harzburg, 22 August 1891 (Haus Dedekind)'. It sits in the 'R.Waermeleitung' bundle as folio 87.

Content of the page: Dedekind finishes an anecdote begun on the previous page. Felix Klein and his wife were in Harzburg a few days earlier. The two men met for only a couple of hours and had an eager mathematical conversation, 'or really more a conversation about mathematicians', from which 'not much of value came out'. Dedekind was nevertheless glad to see Klein so fresh again after 5 years. He hopes the recipient has good news from Nauheim and asks to hear it soon in a nice letter. He sends greetings, also from his sister.

Context from the previous page: Dedekind is sending the recipient fifteen sheets, which he has freshly copied out and ordered historically in red ink. On sheet 9 he discusses the theory of linear partial differential equations; he is not fully sure it is correct, having not thought about it for years. He also mentions papers by Beez printed in Schlömilch's Zeitschrift. He asks for the papers back in Braunschweig in October.

This fits Dedekind's documented collaboration with Heinrich Weber on the 2nd edition of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1892). That edition includes Riemann's Paris prize essay on heat conduction, the 'Commentatio mathematica'. Beez had published on this material, which explains the letter's place in the heat-conduction bundle. That the recipient is Weber is a well-supported inference, not something stated on this page.

No derivation exists to reconstruct.

results.what: Biographical/editorial correspondence: Dedekind (probably to H. Weber), 1891. It concerns material for the edition of Riemann's papers and reports a meeting with Felix Klein in Harzburg.
results.modern_name: Editorial history of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke, 2nd ed. (1892)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a non-mathematical personal letter by Dedekind, written 25 years after Riemann's death. It contains no mathematical results, only editorial and biographical context of minor archival interest.
transcription_corrections: Page author is Richard Dedekind (signed 'R. Dedekind', Harzburg, 22 Aug 1891), not Riemann. The '87' is the archival folio number in the right margin, not part of the text.
First line: 'er verzögert[?] hat' is doubtful. The image shows something closer to 'wo er ... gewandert/verweilt hat'. The reading is uncertain and should stay marked [?].
'Ihn' is written 'Jhn' in the hand (old capital I/J form), referring to Klein.
'mit Frau' and 'Felix Klein' (previous page) are consistent with the image. 'seit 5 Jahren' is confirmed.
